parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the benchers are the senior members who govern each of London's Inns of Court, the barristers' societies

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament lend their backing to the people running a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inn' suggests a pub, but here it means an Inn of Court, one of the four London societies that barristers belong to. Each is run by its benchers.
explanation.definitionFit: Backbench members of Parliament hold no government or shadow office and sit on the rear benches.

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed
wicked means evil

explanation.surface: Conspirators scheme to inflict cruel suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' looks like a scheme, but it is a garden plot, a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or harass someone persistently.

clue.text: Milton's entertainment was rococo music, you see

indicators.note: as you can see, the letters are there in plain sight within the phrase rococo music

explanation.surface: Milton's idea of a good time was ornate eighteenth-century music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You see' points to the letters spanning 'rococO MUSic'. Comus is the masque Milton wrote in 1634, and a masque was a courtly entertainment.
explanation.definitionFit: Comus is John Milton's masque, a staged courtly show of verse, music and dance.

parts.note: the instrument has strings, wires, and its name suggests a newborn that is wonderful just after birth

explanation.surface: A piano is strung soon after it reaches the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivery' reads as a van bringing a piano, but it is childbirth: a baby who is grand, and the piano is wired because it is strung.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small grand piano, the most compact of the horizontal-strung pianos.

definitions.meaning: Oliver Goldsmith, the Irish writer, was nicknamed by this pet form of Oliver

explanation.surface: Goldsmith was supposedly a guardian as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goldsmith' is not a craftsman but Oliver Goldsmith, the eighteenth-century writer; the Protector is Oliver Cromwell. Both were nicknamed with this old pet form of Oliver.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a familiar diminutive of the name Oliver, used for both men.

clue.text: They act as security for house on parts of journey

parts.note: a long journey is divided into stages

explanation.surface: Guards protect a house while its owners travel.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostages are people held as a pledge that terms will be met.

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
a call in bridge is a bid

explanation.surface: A crazy artist is paying a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' suggests a visit, but it is a call in the card game bridge, a bid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means wildly fanatical, or literally infected with rabies, so mad.

clue.text: Sweet-stuff for girl in some distress

indicators.note: in places the girl inside the jumbled letters
distress suggests disorder, so the word some is jumbled

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: Sugary treats are offered to a girl who is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' rearranges SOME into MOES, and 'in' puts LASS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the thick dark syrup left over from refining sugar.

clue.text: It's a holy marvel they left Ireland!

definitions.text: It's a holy marvel they left Ireland!

parts.words: It's a holy marvel they left Ireland!
parts.note: legend says Saint Patrick miraculously drove these reptiles out of the country

explanation.surface: It is a miracle that they emigrated from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'holy marvel' is the legend that Saint Patrick banished all serpents from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland has no native serpents, which legend credits to Saint Patrick.

parts.note: a pair of silent ringers, which in fact are weights for strengthening the arm muscles

explanation.surface: Defective equipment is being stockpiled for a weapons programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arms build-up' reads as military rearmament, but it means building up the muscles of the arms. A dumb bell is one that makes no sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand weights are lifted to develop arm muscle, and their name jokingly describes bells that cannot ring.

definitions.meaning: John ... was Queen Victoria's devoted Scottish attendant
a ... study is a state of absent-minded daydreaming

explanation.surface: A Victorian manservant is at work in the library.
explanation.definitionFit: John Brown served Queen Victoria for decades; to be in a brown study is to be lost in thought.

clue.text: Face possible answer to "When to start school?"

definitions.meaning: the front of the head, countenance

definitions.text: possible answer to "When to start school?"

explanation.surface: A teacher confronts the question of what age children should begin their education.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the Roman numeral for five, the age at which British children start school, so 'V is age' answers the question.
explanation.definitionFit: A visage is a person's face or countenance, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Tough assignment for both helmsman and trencherman

definitions.text: Tough assignment for both helmsman and trencherman

parts.words: Tough assignment for both helmsman and trencherman
parts.note: for the steersman a difficult change of sailing course, and for the hearty eater a ship's biscuit that is hard to chew

explanation.surface: A demanding job challenges both the ship's steersman and the big eater aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: A trencherman is a hearty eater; hardtack is the hard dry biscuit once eaten at sea, while for the helmsman a 'hard tack' would be a difficult turn into the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardtack is a plain flour-and-water biscuit baked very hard to keep on long voyages.

definitions.meaning: someone who is not a clergyman, an ordinary member of the congregation
Thomas Babington Macaulay wrote the Lays of Ancient Rome, so he is a man of lays

explanation.surface: Macaulay was certainly no clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay was a Victorian historian and poet whose best-known verse collection is the Lays of Ancient Rome; a lay is a narrative poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A layman is a non-clergyman; split, the word suggests a writer of lays, which Macaulay was.

clue.text: Cavalry of the old order nary a reform

parts.note: ye is an old spelling of the
OM is the Order of Merit

indicators.note: to reform is to make again, so the letters of nary are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Old-style horse soldiers resist any reorganisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reform' rearranges NARY into ANRY. 'Of the old order' reads as a phrase, but 'the old' gives YE and 'order' gives OM.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeomanry were volunteer cavalry regiments raised from farmers and landowners.

definitions.meaning: red in the political sense, socialists or communists

explanation.surface: Left-handed boxers are compared with red-faced politicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' means red, and red is the colour of the political left. A southpaw is a left-handed boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word suggests people who favour their left hand, and it is the usual term for radical left-wing politicians.

clue.text: Revolutionary form of punishment for foot-sloggers

definitions.text: Revolutionary form of punishment for foot-sloggers

parts.words: Revolutionary form of punishment for foot-sloggers
parts.note: a turning wheel climbed endlessly by prisoners as a penalty

explanation.surface: Infantry face a radical new penalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' suggests political upheaval but means turning round; Victorian prisoners walked a rotating wheel as punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The treadmill was a wheel prisoners trod to keep it turning, as a penal labour.

indicators.note: replacement means the letters of Dean Tate are moved into new places

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A dean expects to be named Tate's successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replacement' rearranges the letters of DEAN TATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To antedate is to come before or forestall, an older sense of anticipate.

clue.text: His ship plays security role in war

definitions.text: His ship plays security role in war

parts.words: His ship plays security role in war
parts.note: add the word ship to this official and you get the wartime cutting of letters and news to protect secrets

explanation.surface: A captain's vessel guards the convoy during wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His ship' is not a vessel: it is the suffix -ship added to the official's title, making the wartime practice of suppressing information.
explanation.definitionFit: A censor examines mail and press reports and removes anything that could help the enemy.

definitions.meaning: sorts again, puts into a fresh arrangement
spas and seaside towns visited for health and recreation

explanation.surface: A firm rearranges its spas.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as re-sorts, the word means sorts again.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-sorting is arranging afresh; resorts are places people visit for rest or health.

clue.text: Oddly enough he's a card at indoor games

indicators.note: said of letters that end up in an odd, unexpected arrangement, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, the joker at the party is a real card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly enough' rearranges the letters of HE'S A CARD; 'card' in the surface means a comic person.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a parlour game of acting out words or titles syllable by syllable for others to guess.

indicators.note: the letters of hears are forced awkwardly into a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Jacobson is hard of hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacobson' looks like a surname, but it means a son of Jacob: Asher was one of Jacob's twelve sons.
explanation.definitionFit: Asher was the eighth son of the patriarch Jacob, founder of one of Israel's tribes.

clue.text: Put on a service, say, for the goggling customers

indicators.note: say tells us the phrase is spoken, so its sound matters rather than its spelling

parts.note: to put on is to add, and a church service is a mass, giving add mass

explanation.surface: A church lays on an extra service to attract the gawping public.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add mass' (put on a service) said out loud gives the word for the mass public that advertising targets.
explanation.definitionFit: The term names the mass audience swayed by advertising and television, pictured staring at the screen.

clue.text: A right that is not one's own

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: Someone has a legal claim to property that belongs to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign, belonging to someone or somewhere else.

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
EC, East Central, is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: A part of town works for a fuel company.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'combine' is a cartel: here the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries. EC is the postcode area of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: This organization groups oil-producing nations that coordinate output and prices, a cartel.

parts.note: a Lar is a Roman household god
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A tree spirit keeps distinguished company.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lares were the Roman gods of the household; CH, Companion of Honour, is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer, a familiar forest tree.

parts.note: a component fitted into a radio or sound system to make it louder, not to make a book fatter

explanation.surface: A section is inserted to make a book thicker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' suggests a book, and 'part inset' suggests extra pages; in fact volume is loudness and the part is an electronic component.
explanation.definitionFit: This device boosts an electrical signal so that the sound produced is louder.

clue.text: Never missed date in Athens, for example

definitions.text: missed date in Athens, for example
definitions.meaning: the calends, first day of the Roman month, did not exist in the Greek calendar

explanation.surface: An appointment in Athens was never kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The calends were Roman, not Greek, so something put off to the Greek calends will never happen.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means a time that will never come, since the Greeks had no calends.
